pageCache.pageTitle: Birdlip Primary School Gloucester - Home Page
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Birdlip Primary School
Birdlip School is a fabulous village school. Nestled in the picturesque Cotswolds and only a short distance from Cheltenham and Gloucester, we cater for children aged 4-11, in 4 separate classes. At an altitude of over 980 feet, we take pride in being at the top of everything that we do. Our children come from Birdlip village and the surrounding areas.
We are passionate that every child should fulfil the best of their own potential and have a happy, enjoyable time at Birdlip with lots of fun! Our ethos is centered around our three key values - Respect, Resilience and Kindness.
Birdlip school is a caring, safe community in which children and adults are treated with respect. We want every member of the school community to be happy, healthy, eager to learn, confident in their own abilities and generous in the recognition of others.
We encourage our pupils on their individual learning journeys to explore areas of knowledge with an open mind and open heart, to debate, challenge, be creative, exchange opinions and ideas and in doing so reach their full potential.
We have an unshakeable belief that given the right support all pupils can succeed and we aim to make that happen; we want to help each child prepare for a bigger world!
Headteacher is Mr James Pugh
Chair of Governors: Mr Phill Hastings-Jones

pageCache.text:
Our Aims, Values and Ethos
"Helping each other to prepare for a bigger world"
At Birdlip School we strive hard to develop the school as a caring, safe community in which children and adults are treated with respect. We want every member of the community to be happy, healthy, eager to learn, confident in their own abilities and generous in the recognition of others. We are passionate that every child should fulfil the best of their potential.
We encourage the children to explore areas of knowledge with an open mind, develop the ability to exchange opinions and ideas, to relish the new challenges given and do as well as they possibly can.
We will give the children first hand experiences by taking them out on educational visits and bringing speakers and artifacts into school.
We will develop the children's imagination through different creative media and help them to achieve good health, physical development, co-ordination and enjoyment through physical education.
All children and staff have the right to feel safe at all times in school. There should be mutual respect between staff and children and between each other. All visitors to the school should feel safe and free from the effects of poor behaviour at all times and in all parts of the school.
Our philosophy is to promote positive behaviour and a zest for learning. Our core values resilience, respect and kindness are a key focus to our end of week assembly.
A28 Written Statement of Behaviour Principles

Reading
At Birdlip, reading and the teaching of reading skills is the foundation of our curriculum. Our aim is to ensure every single child becomes primary literate and progresses in the areas of reading, speaking and listening.
We want to equip them with not only the minimum statutory requirements of the Reading National Curriculums but to provide literature and opportunities to discuss literature that will prepare them for the bigger world and experiences of later life. We want to use books to explore culture, diversity, gender and instil a cultural capital in our children.
Reading begins with phonics in reception and Year 1 - we use the Read, Write, inc scheme - and progresses using a reading scheme focusing on key skills such as inference and recall. In KS1 and KS2 we use whole class guided reading to read a plethora of genres and content and work through key reading skills to improve comprehension.
‘I love stories!’ EYFS
‘’It makes me happy’ Y1
‘It makes me calm and loved’ Y1
‘Excited, fun, joyful’ Y2
‘I read to myself, sometimes I laugh and I cry sometimes’ Y2
‘Relaxed, happy, tired, warm Y2’
‘Really excited to turn the second page.’ Y2
‘It’s like a new world to explore.’ Y3
‘Happy and calm because I get some time on my own.’ Y3
‘Happy, excited, emotional and sometimes I feel like I’m inside the story.’ Y4
‘I’m there in the story and it’s calming’ Y4
‘It makes me hooked into the book’ Y5
‘It makes me feel adventurous’ Y5
‘It makes me feel I’m in the world they are in’ Y6
‘It hooks me in because your brain takes in the images of the book’ Y6
‘It makes me a lot calmer’ Y6
Whole Class Guided Reading at Birdlip
At Birdlip we use whole-class guided reading from Year 1 up to Y6. We use stimulating and challenging texts aimed to help pupil’s love of reading.
Whole class guided reading is also used to expand pupils' vocabulary and deepen their understanding of the texts they are reading. We do this through explicit teaching of vocabulary before reading the text and re-reading sections looking closely at the elements which require further understanding. Across a week of guided reading, we develop the pupil's retrieval, prediction, summarising, inference and author's choice.
Guided Reading Curriculum Plan
Story Time at Birdlip
At Birdlip we recognise the importance of having a story read to the pupils every day across all ages. It contributes towards developing a love of books and enhances pupil’s wellbeing.
In EYFS and KS1, we read a variety of picture books with some class novels in Y1 and 2. In KS2, we often use extracts for whole class guided reading for longer books and story time gives the pupils a chance to hear and get to know the whole novel.
School Library
We have an extensive library with a good selection of fiction and non fiction books for all ages. All pupils have access top the library once a week.
We have a section called ‘Birdlip Curriculum’ where pupils can borrow a copy of the whole class guided reading book. Pupils can also access the Virtual Library to read books used in whole class guided reading.
We have a reading assembly every week based in the library where pupils will read and recommend books to others.
Our Year 6 librarians have the responsibility of looking after the library and keeping it up-to-date.
The Birdlip Primary School Virtual Library
We use a virtual library to provide your child with a source of high quality reading books whilst they are away from school. Each class has their own page with books which are taught across the curriculum and are age-appropriate. The slideshow below shows you what the class pages look like and which books are available.
To access the Virtual Library, you will need to download the Virtual Library Powerpoint document shown below, (open and set it to play slideshow) navigate to your child's class page and click on a book cover which will take you to either a book, an audio book or an extract.
As a school, we are often asked by parents and carers which books children should be reading at their age and so we hope this will help in selecting appropriate new books for your child.
Other Suggested Reading
Children are encouraged to read to an adult at least three times a week at home and we would also like to recommend that parents frequently read to/with their children until they are teenagers.
It is important to understand that reading is not merely sounding words or “blending” (this is phonics) but the combination of the following skills, using the acrostic VIPERS
